description: STOP RUN WITH status phrase, ISO §2023:14.9.42 — the status phrase is a COBOL-2002 introduction. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): the 1985 STOP statement is STOP RUN or STOP literal-1, with no status operand (§1985:VI.6.24.4 GR1: 'If the RUN phrase is specified, execution of the run unit ceases and control is transferred to the operating system'; GR4: 'If STOP literal-1 is specified, the execution of the run unit is suspended and literal-1 is communicated to the operator'); §2002:14.8.38.3 GR5 reads 'During execution of the STOP statement with literal-1 or identifier-1 specified, literal-1 or the contents of the data item referenced by identifier-1 are passed to the operating system', and §2002:F.2 states the change, its item 131: 'The WITH STATUS phrase was added to the STOP statement to allow a run unit to return a value to the operating system.' §2014:14.9.38.3 GR5 carries it, so 2014 = 2023.
